newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Private debts to S.Africa's Eskom soar.
newsitem.headline: Private debts to S.Africa's Eskom soar.

text.p: Private consumer debts to South Africa's state-owned Eskom electricity company have more than doubled to 847 million rand over the past two years, Provincial Affairs Minister Mohammed Valli Moosa said on Tuesday.
The figure was amongst details revealed in a briefing for journalists and investors on the financial viability of South Africa's 811 municipalities.

"The outstanding debt owed by individual consumers to Eskom in areas where it is the direct supplier has steadily increased from 147 million rand in December 1993 to 847 million rand as at January 31, 1997," Valli Moosa said in a written report.
The debt total was 361 million rand in December 1994 and 575 million rand a year later.
"It must be borne in mind that Eskom has recently provided electricity to a much wider range of consumers, which could explain the sharp increase in the default amount," he said.
Municipalities act as agents for Eskom in many areas, but the trend with new installations is for the utility to bill clients directly.
Valli Moosa estimated that about a third of municipalities were viable and able to exercise sound fiscal control, about a third were "stressed" and about a third were "not viable".
He said the Local Authorities Loans Fund experienced its first default in its 18-year history at the end of June 1995.
By the end of 1996, however, 48 municipalities were in default, though the nine million rand total owed represented barely one percent of the 880 million rand loan book.
Valli Moosa said the total owed to local authorities had risen from five billion rand in June 1995 to six billion rand in October last year.

He said that though the number of municipal accounts paid regularly had not risen above 68 percent in the past year, he believed the South African local government financing crisis had "bottomed out" and that the situation was improving.

"We now have a macro picture of the state of local government financing. It tells us that the situation is far from satisfactory, but we don't think the situation is deteriorating at this time," he said.
